body.explanation: Greater stretch of the myocardium leads to a stronger contraction, within physiological limits.

title: Indicate the correct propositions regarding the Compliance of the Lung (C)

options: The compliance of the lung tells us how easy it is for the lungs to move air volumes in and out for a given level of transpulmonary pressure
The compliance of the lung can be calculated as the ratio of the change in lung volume (DV) for each unit change in transpulmonary pressure (DP)
The compliance of the lung is the same during inspiration and during expiration
The compliance of the lung is greater during inspiration than during expiration
The compliance of the lung is greater during expiration than during inspiration

The parasympathetic system slows down the heart rate (causing bradycardia)

title: Hydrochloric acid in the stomach is secreted by:
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Hydrochloric acid in the stomach is secreted by:
body.explanation: Parietal (oxyntic) cells secrete HCl and intrinsic factor; chief cells secrete pepsinogen; G cells secrete gastrin.

title: Indicate the characteristics of the systemic circulation
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Indicate the characteristics of the systemic circulation
options: It provides oxygen rich arterial blood to all organs of the human body
It brings carbon dioxide rich venous blood back to the lungs
The pressure in the systemic circulation is higher than the one found in the pulmonary circulation
The resistance in the systemic circulation is lower than the one found in the pulmonary circulation
It accounts for more than 80% of total blood volume of the human body

title: Hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction:
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction:
options: Happens in systemic arteries as well
Dilates vessels in poorly ventilated areas to match perfusion
Diverts blood away from poorly ventilated alveoli
body.explanation: Unlike systemic vessels, pulmonary vessels constrict in hypoxia, matching perfusion to ventilation.

title: Cardiac output equals:
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Cardiac output equals:
body.explanation: CO = HR × SV (≈ 70 × 70 mL ≈ 5 L/min).

title: Indicate the correct propositions regarding Hypoxic Pulmonary Vasoconstriction (HPV)
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Indicate the correct propositions regarding Hypoxic Pulmonary Vasoconstriction (HPV)
options: Hypoxic Pulmonary Vasoconstriction (HPV) spontaneously occurs in human lungs when the level of alveolar oxygen is very low (alveolar hypoxia)
Hypoxic Pulmonary Vasoconstriction (HPV) is a protective effect allowing optimization of pulmonary gas exchange in situations where alveolar ventilation is insufficient
The protective effect of Hypoxic Pulmonary Vasoconstriction (HPV) is related to the fact that blood is diverted from normal alveolar region to poorly oxygenated alveolar area
Hypoxic Pulmonary Vasoconstriction (HPV) is never seen in the fetal lungs
Hypoxic Pulmonary Vasoconstriction (HPV) is often seen in people leaving at high altitude

title: Indicate the correct propositions regarding cardiac output
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Indicate the correct propositions regarding cardiac output
options: Cardiac output can be calculated by adding stroke volume to the heart rate
Cardiac output can be calculated by dividing stroke volume to the heart rate
Cardiac output can be calculated by multiplying stroke volume to the heart rate
In order to maintain cardiac output in a failing heart with reduced stroke volume, one can decrease the heart rate (bradycardia)
In order to maintain cardiac output in a failing heart with reduced stroke volume, one can increase the heart rate (tachycardia)

title: Hormones secreted by the anterior pituitary include:
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Hormones secreted by the anterior pituitary include:
options: TSH, ACTH, GH, prolactin, FSH and LH
body.explanation: ADH and oxytocin are made in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary.

title: Indicate the correct propositions regarding the physiological role of the surfactant

body.stem: Indicate the correct propositions regarding the physiological role of the surfactant
options: The surfactant reduces alveolar surface tension especially in alveoli with small diameters
The surfactant keeps alveolar pressure at the same level in all alveoli irrespective of their sizes
Lack of surfactant favors collapses of small alveoli and the occurrence of respiratory distress syndrome in premature babies
Lack of surfactant decreases lung compliance
Lack of surfactant increases lung compliance

body.stem: Indicate the correct propositions regarding blood gas transport
options: The relationship between the amount of O dissolved in the plasma and the saturation of hemoglobin (Hb) is called the oxygen-hemoglobin saturation curve
A shift of the oxygen-hemoglobin saturation curve to the right means that it is easier to unload (release) O at the tissue level

options: The Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) is the volume of air which stays in the lungs after a full and maximal expiration
The Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) is the volume of air which stays in the lungs after normal and quiet expiration
The Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) cannot be measured by normal spirometry
The Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) is one component of the Vital Capacity (VC)
The Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) is one component of the Total Lung Capacity (TLC)

title: Indicate the correct propositions regarding stroke volume
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Indicate the correct propositions regarding stroke volume
options: The stroke volume is the volume of blood pumped from the left or the right ventricle per heartbeat

The stroke volume is calculated by subtracting the volume of the blood in the ventricle at the end of systole (called end-systolic volume) from the volume of blood at the end of diastole (called end-diastolic volume)
The end-systolic volume is the highest volume of blood in the ventricle at any point in the cardiac cycle
The end-diastolic volume is the lowest volume of blood in the ventricle at any point in the cardiac cycle
The stroke volume can be modified by changing either end-diastolic volume or end-systolic volume or both

body.stem: Secretin mainly stimulates:
options: Pancreatic enzyme secretion from the acinar cells
body.explanation: Secretin (from S cells, released by acid in the duodenum) causes bicarbonate-rich pancreatic juice; CCK drives enzymes and gallbladder contraction.

title: Indicate the characteristics of the pulmonary circulation
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Indicate the characteristics of the pulmonary circulation
options: It provides oxygen poor arterial blood to alveolar regions of the lungs
It provides carbon dioxide rich arterial blood to alveolar regions of the lungs
The pressure in the pulmonary circulation is higher than the one found in the systemic circulation
The pulmonary blood flow is equal to the cardiac output

body.explanation: SGLT1 (Na+-glucose cotransport) apically; GLUT2 basolaterally. Fructose uses GLUT5.

The cardiac output can be increased with increased stroke volume (with a strong heart) whilst keeping heart rate unchanged
The cardiac output can be increased by keeping stroke volume unchanged whilst lowering heart rate (bradycardia)

title: The pulmonary circulation is a:
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: The pulmonary circulation is a:
options: Low-flow system receiving 10% of the cardiac output
System with a mean pressure of about 90 mmHg
body.explanation: Mean pulmonary artery pressure ≈ 15 mmHg; it receives the whole right ventricular output.

Alveolar volume (VA) can be greater than the tidal volume (VT)
The tidal volume (VT) is the addition of alveolar volume (VA) and the dead space (VD)

The stroke volume can be increased by increasing end-systolic volume with end-diastolic volume kept unchanged
The stroke volume can be increased by increasing end-diastolic volume and decreasing end-systolic volume
The stroke volume can be increased by decreasing end-diastolic volume and decreasing end-systolic volume

title: The normal pacemaker of the heart is:

body.stem: The normal pacemaker of the heart is:
body.explanation: The SA node has the fastest intrinsic rate (≈60-100/min) and sets the rhythm.

title: Indicate the correct propositions regarding the Vital Capacity (VC)
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Indicate the correct propositions regarding the Vital Capacity (VC)
options: The Vital Capacity (VC) represents the total amount of volumes of air that are in the lungs of a living subject
The Vital Capacity (VC) represents the total amount of volumes of air that can be exchanged with the environment during an intense physical exercise
Vital Capacity is the addition of three ‘elementary’ volumes, namely the Tidal Volume (VT), the Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV) and the Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV)
The addition of the Vital Capacity (VC) to the Residual Volume (RV) gives the Total Lung Capacity (TLC)
The Vital Capacity is reduced in many respiratory diseases including lung fibrosis, asthma, and COPD

title: Most circulating thyroid hormone is:
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Most circulating thyroid hormone is:
options: Free T3, the active form in plasma
T4 bound to plasma proteins (mainly TBG)
body.explanation: Over 99% is protein-bound; T4 is the main secreted form and is converted to the active T3 in tissues.

title: Indicate the correct propositions regarding the Residual Volume (RV)
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Indicate the correct propositions regarding the Residual Volume (RV)
options: The Residual Volume (RV) is the volume of air which stays in the lungs after a full and maximal expiration
The Residual Volume (RV) is the volume of air which stays in the lungs after normal and quiet expiration
The Residual Volume (RV) cannot be measured by normal spirometry
The Residual Volume (RV) is one component of the Vital Capacity (VC)
The Residual Volume (RV) is one component of the Total Lung Capacity (TLC)

title: Which substance does NOT stimulate acid secretion by parietal cells?
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Which substance does NOT stimulate acid secretion by parietal cells?
body.explanation: Somatostatin inhibits acid secretion; ACh, gastrin and histamine stimulate it.

title: Indicate the principal components of the cardiovascular system

options: The blood components (the fluid to be moved)

subject: subj:physio1

Residual volume and Functional Residual Capacity are increased

title: Which volume cannot be measured by simple spirometry?
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Which volume cannot be measured by simple spirometry?
body.explanation: Residual volume (and so FRC and TLC) needs helium dilution, nitrogen washout or plethysmography.

title: Indicate the correct propositions regarding high blood pressure
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Indicate the correct propositions regarding high blood pressure
options: High blood pressure can result from increased vascular resistance to maintain blood flow
High blood pressure can result from decreased vascular resistance when blood flow is unchanged
High blood pressure can increase blood flow when vascular resistance is unchanged
High blood pressure increases when the diameter of the vessels increases (vasodilation)
High blood pressure increases when the diameter of the vessels decreases (vasoconstriction)

title: During isovolumetric contraction:
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: During isovolumetric contraction:
options: Ventricular volume falls quickly as blood is ejected
All valves are closed and ventricular pressure rises
body.explanation: Between closure of the AV valves (S1) and opening of the semilunar valves.

title: The migrating motor complex (MMC):
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: The migrating motor complex (MMC):
options: Happens during fasting and sweeps residue through the small bowel
Happens mainly after meals and mixes chyme with digestive enzymes
body.explanation: MMCs are fasting 'housekeeper' waves, linked to motilin.

title: On the ECG, the QRS complex represents:
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: On the ECG, the QRS complex represents:
options: Conduction through the AV node only
body.explanation: P = atrial depolarisation, QRS = ventricular depolarisation, T = ventricular repolarisation.

title: Vital capacity equals:
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Vital capacity equals:
options: Functional residual capacity + residual volume − tidal volume
Tidal volume + inspiratory reserve volume + expiratory reserve volume
body.explanation: VC = TV + IRV + ERV; TLC = VC + RV.

title: Most water absorption in the gut happens in:
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Most water absorption in the gut happens in:
body.explanation: About 80% of water is absorbed in the small intestine; the colon absorbs most of the rest.

title: A normal PR interval is:
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: A normal PR interval is:
body.explanation: PR > 0.20 s = first-degree AV block.

title: Indicate the correct propositions regarding the cardiac node cells
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Indicate the correct propositions regarding the cardiac node cells
options: The cardiac node cells are made by specialized cells capable of automaticity, called pacemaker cells
The cardiac node cells can be found in the sinoatrial (SA) node and the atrioventricular (AV) node
The cardiac node cells are not present in the Purkinjie fibers
In a healthy heart the AV node is the pacemaker and controls the electrical impulses which cause contraction
The pace of the SA node, being higher than the one of the AV node, is the one controlling the physiological heart rate

title: Indicate the physiological functions of the human lungs
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Indicate the physiological functions of the human lungs
options: Gas exchange between the breathing air and the pulmonary circulation
Removal of carbon dioxide from the blood

title: Indicate the correct propositions regarding the physiological roles of the atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) in the cardiovascular system
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: Indicate the correct propositions regarding the physiological roles of the atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) in the cardiovascular system
options: Atrial Natriuretic Peptide (ANP) is synthesized and secreted by cardiac muscle cells in the walls of the atria in the heart
Synthesis of ANP is stimulated by cardiac distention
Synthesis of ANP is stimulated by sympathetic stimulation
ANP causes vasodilation and reduces blood pressure
ANP reduces renal elimination of sodium (reducing natriuresis)

title: The plateau phase (phase 2) of the ventricular action potential is mainly due to:
subject: subj:physio1

body.stem: The plateau phase (phase 2) of the ventricular action potential is mainly due to:
options: Fast Na+ entry through voltage-gated channels that stay open
Slow Ca2+ entry through L-type channels balanced by K+ exit
body.explanation: L-type Ca2+ influx balances K+ efflux, prolonging the action potential and the refractory period.
